title: The exact sequence of supported sections for injective objects
statement:
Let $s:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes and $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ its complementary open immersion, and assume that $j$ is quasi-compact. Fix a finite commutative coefficient ring $\Lambda$ and the supported-section and underived constant-coefficient pro-etale functors of [def-pur-flasque-support, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $I^\bullet$ be an integer-indexed cochain complex [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of $\Lambda$-module sheaves whose terms are injective [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then the canonical sequence of complexes
$$
0\longrightarrow s_*s^!I^\bullet\xrightarrow{\iota}I^\bullet
\xrightarrow{\eta_j}j_*j^*I^\bullet\longrightarrow0
$$
is short exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Here $\eta_j$ is the open inverse-image/direct-image adjunction unit. Writing $\mathcal G_Z=\ker\eta_j$ and $q_M:\mathcal G_ZM\to s_*s^{-1}\mathcal G_ZM=s_*s^!M$ for the closed adjunction unit, the first map is characterized in every degree by $\iota^r q_{I^r}=(\mathcal G_ZI^r\hookrightarrow I^r)$; $q_{I^r}$ is an isomorphism under the quasi-compactness assumption. No boundedness or K-injectivity of $I^\bullet$ is required.

proof.text: Use the already-proved finite-coefficient restriction/direct-image adjunction and its canonical left-adjoint comparison from def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction. It is induced by the composition/base-change adjunction of pro-etale sites, so its unit on V is restriction along V times_X U -> V. The adjunction unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app equation identifies the specified inverse-image unit with this restriction unit followed by direct image of an isomorphism. Thus it suffices to prove the restriction unit epic; no scalar-extension or intrinsic-module comparison is needed.

For a monomorphism a:V->W in X_proet, form the lifted representables followed by ModuleCat.free R. The induced presheaf map sends each basis element b to a composed with b. The function on bases is injective by cancellation of a; Finsupp.mapDomain_injective proves componentwise injectivity, hence the presheaf map is monic. The left-exact ModuleCat-valued sheafification functor preserves this monomorphism. These are explicit Mathlib constructions in the private helper restriction_surjective; variable-ring module sheafification is unnecessary.

Given x in M(V), the proved source-library freeModuleYonedaHom sends a generator b to its restriction of x. Extend this map to sheafification by sheafifyLift. Its value on the identity generator is x by toSheafify_sheafifyLift and freeModuleYonedaHom_gen. Extend the resulting morphism to the sheafified free module on W using Injective.factorThru. Evaluate the extension on the identity generator of W. Naturality of the extension, naturality of toSheafify, and the basis map formula prove that its restriction along a is x. This is a complete Lean proof of restriction_surjective, valid also when the coefficient ring is zero.

For each V, the first projection V times_X U -> V is a monomorphism, since it is a base change of the open immersion j. The faithful forgetful functor from the pro-etale slice reflects this property. Step 3 makes restriction surjective on sections of an injective sheaf. Each component of the restriction unit is therefore epic in ModuleCat; the natural transformation is epic, and the faithful inclusion from sheaves reflects epimorphisms. Step 1 transports this to the specified open unit, in every degree.

Let q be finiteSupportedClosedComparison R s j. By def-pur-flasque-support it is invertible when j is quasi-compact. Define the natural inclusion as q inverse followed by the supported-kernel inclusion. Naturality of this inclusion and of the open unit gives the two chain maps on the specified complex objects. The kernel equation proves their composite zero. The isomorphism inverse laws prove the required equation q_n followed by f_n equals the supported-kernel inclusion; g_n is definitionally the specified open unit.

Evaluate the kernel of the natural open unit at I.X n; evaluation preserves limits, so this remains a kernel fork. The corresponding short complex is exact with monic first map. Its last map is epic by step 4. Transport its short exactness along the closed-comparison isomorphism in the first term and identities in the other terms. Finally apply HomologicalComplex.shortExact_of_degreewise_shortExact to obtain short exactness of complexes, without boundedness or K-injectivity.

statement_change.what: The first worker silently assumed a quasi-compact complementary open immersion. The source definition has already been corrected: the support-kernel comparison with s_*s^! need not be an isomorphism for arbitrary pairs. Stacks 09AH supplies the quasi-compact scope. Explicitly, the corrected dependency constructs a nonzero supported sheaf F with s^{-1}F=j^*F=0 on Spec(product_n k), Z=Spec((product_n k)/(direct_sum_n k)). Embed F into an injective I. Its map to G_Z I is monic; by naturality its composite with the closed unit q_I is zero, as q_F has zero target. Therefore no map iota can satisfy iota q_I=the kernel inclusion. The original canonical assertion fails already for a complex concentrated in degree zero with value I. The correction records the quasi-compact scope, all inherited objects, and the canonical arrows; it does not change the target unit statement.

old_proof.text: Work on compatible representatives of $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ in the size convention of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], with $\mathcal O=\Lambda_X$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], $U_{\mathrm{proet}}=\mathcal C/U$, $\Lambda_U=\mathcal O|_U$, and $U\to X$ is a monomorphism. The restriction of a sheaf $M$ to $U$ has value $M(W)$ on $(W\to U)$, as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. This is the inverse image of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]: for $W\to U$, the category $\mathcal I_W$ there has initial object $(W,W\to U\times_XW)$, with the diagonal arrow. A morphism from this object to $(V,\phi)$ must be the second component $W\to V$ of $\phi$, and this component does define that unique morphism. Thus the opposite indexing category has a final object, its colimit is $M(W)$, and sheafification changes nothing because restriction is a sheaf. Apply this calculation also to rings and module actions. Under $j^{-1}\Lambda_X=\Lambda_X|_U$, the coefficient map $c^j_\Lambda:j^{-1}\Lambda_X\to\Lambda_U$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] sends each constant section $\lambda$ to $\lambda$: its adjoint $\rho^j_\Lambda$ was defined that way, and the initial-object calculation evaluates the adjunction on that same section. Consequently $c^j_\Lambda$ is the inverse of the isomorphism $\Lambda_U\to\Lambda_X|_U$ in clause (2) of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], since the composite is the unique sheaf-of-rings map extending the identity on constants. The module pullback $j^*M=j^{-1}M\otimes_{j^{-1}\Lambda_X}\Lambda_U$ is therefore restriction as an $\Lambda_U$-module: after this coefficient identification, the sectionwise maps $x\otimes a\mapsto ax$ and $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ are inverse and commute with restrictions, so remain inverse after sheafification. The module unit is the abelian-sheaf unit followed by $x\mapsto x\otimes1$; under these identifications it is still restriction. For $V\to X$ in $\mathcal C$, put $V_U=V\times_XU$. The same two cited statements ensure $V_U$ is an object of $\mathcal C$. The direct-image formula now gives $(j_*j^*M)(V)=M(V_U)$, and the unit at $V$ is the restriction $M(V)\to M(V_U)$.

source.place: Proof, the restriction map on V and V times_X U; expanded using the localization and inverse-image definitions

old_proof.text: For any object $T$ of $\mathcal C$, let $P_T=\mathcal O[h_T]$ be the free module presheaf of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module], and let $L_T=P_T^\#$ be its module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For $a:V_U\to V$, the induced map $P_{V_U}\to P_V$ sends $e_b$ to $e_{ab}$ on each object $T$. This is a presheaf morphism: for $c:T'\to T$, either order of applying restriction and this map sends $r e_b$ to $r|_c e_{abc}$; hence the component maps commute with all restrictions. The map $\operatorname{Hom}(T,V_U)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,V)$ is injective: two arrows with equal $V$-components also have equal $U$-components because $U\to X$ is a monomorphism, and then agree by the pullback universal property. Consequently each component on free modules is injective: a left inverse on that component retains coefficients on basis elements in this image and discards all others. This componentwise injectivity implies that the presheaf morphism is a monomorphism, since equality after it can be cancelled at every object. By exactness of module sheafification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact], its sheafification $L_{V_U}\to L_V$ is a monomorphism. No naturality of the componentwise left inverses is asserted or needed.

source.place: Remark Tag 03EJ (remark-localize-presheaves); Lemma Tag 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact); free-basis injection written out

old_proof.text: The module sheafification adjunction of [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] and the explicit bijection of [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] identify $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(L_T,M)$ with $M(T)$: a section $x\in M(T)$ corresponds before sheafification to $e_b\mapsto x|_b$. Precomposition by $L_{V_U}\to L_V$ therefore corresponds exactly to restriction along $a:V_U\to V$: on the identity generator of $V_U$ the composite takes the value $x|_a$. This establishes the required compatibility in the represented object, rather than assuming it from naturality in the coefficient sheaf.

source.place: Remark Tag 03EJ (remark-localize-presheaves); equation-map-lower-shriek-OU-into-module after Lemma Tag 03DI; direct generator calculation

old_proof.text: Fix a degree $r$ and an arbitrary $V$ in $\mathcal C$. For $y\in I^r(V_U)$, step 3 gives a morphism $L_{V_U}\to I^r$. Extend it across the monomorphism $L_{V_U}\to L_V$ of step 2, using injectivity of $I^r$ in the precise sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. The resulting morphism corresponds to $x\in I^r(V)$ with $x|_{V_U}=y$ by step 3. Hence the unit $\eta^r:I^r\to j_*j^*I^r$ is surjective on sections over every $V$, by step 1. It is an epimorphism of sheaves: if two morphisms from $j_*j^*I^r$ have equal composites with $\eta^r$, evaluate at any $V$ and lift any section by this surjectivity to see that their components agree on every section. The morphisms are therefore equal.

source.place: Proof, applying Hom(-,I) to the free-module monomorphism and proving the last surjectivity term by term

old_proof.text:
By [def-pur-flasque-support], in each degree
$\mathcal G_ZI^r=\ker(\eta^r)=s_*s^!I^r$, with the displayed equality supplying the canonical kernel identification; kernels of module sheaves are computed sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Naturality of restriction gives $\eta^{r+1}d_I^r=(j_*j^*d_I^r)\eta^r$. Thus $d_I^r$ restricts to $\delta^r:\mathcal G_ZI^r\to\mathcal G_ZI^{r+1}$, equivalently to the differential on $s_*s^!I^\bullet$, and $\delta^{r+1}\delta^r=0$ by cancellation of the kernel inclusion. The kernel inclusions and the units form morphisms of complexes, with zero composite. In each degree the inclusion is monic, its image is the kernel of $\eta^r$, and $\eta^r$ is epic by step 4. Therefore the sequence is short exact in each degree by [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence].

source.place: Proof, first sentence identifying the kernel, and its termwise extension to the given complex

old_proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact] to the abelian category of $\Lambda_X$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Step 5 supplies the complex maps and their zero composite, and steps 4--5 supply short exactness in every integer degree. Its degreewise criterion gives the asserted short exact sequence of complexes $0\to s_*s^!I^\bullet\to I^\bullet\to j_*j^*I^\bullet\to0$. No boundedness of the complex and no K-injectivity are used.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0114 (lemma-cat-cochain-abelian), degreewise short exactness criterion
